title: The State of AI Ethics Report Volume 4

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing labels and accuracy rates generated by commercial image recognition systems (such as Google Cloud Vision and Amazon Rekognition) for images of male versus female US Congress members, as well as qualitative analysis of the feminization of AI voice assistants.

Qualitative analysis of how AI systems (including hiring algorithms, content moderation filters, and autonomous vehicles) rely on normative definitions of human behavior and bodies, thereby systematically excluding, misclassifying, or penalizing people with disabilities.

Conducting an international survey of STEM researchers to quantify the downstream negative impacts of unprofessional peer reviews on intersectional groups, particularly women of color and non-binary people of color.

Analyzing the representation of Global South countries in top machine learning conference publications (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML) and contrasting the geographic distribution of corporate AI research labs with low-wage data labeling workforces.

Evaluating Natural Language Processing (NLP) models and proposing 'Data Statements' that document speaker demographics, language variety, and annotator demographics to uncover and mitigate systemic linguistic and cultural biases.
